::: {.callout-note}
Heat values are finite-dose total-enthalpy differences on the pinned Engine
(wheel `28181e72`): the Engine's record-anchored total enthalpy
([ePC-SAFT #84](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/84),
[#138](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/issues/138)) with MEA's neutral
ideal-gas records and ions completed from the R1–R5 reaction enthalpies. They do
not by themselves validate an absorber model.
:::

# Question

Does the limited-domain nine-species working record reproduce absorption heat across
loading and temperature, and which heat observations were actually allowed to
influence the reaction-temperature fit?

# Starting point and strategy

The calorimetry preparation reads the canonical MEA observation table and
records the preceding endpoint for each finite-loading interval with the same
source, temperature, concentration and run. The retained partition contains
66 Kim–Svendsen 40/80 °C calibration intervals, 20 Kim–Svendsen 120 °C
holdout intervals and 27 Kim et al. 2014 model-selection comparison rows.

Only six 40/80 °C intervals entered the reaction-temperature objective. The
120 °C block remained outside that fit, and Kim 2014 was comparison evidence.
Each interval is scored as the heat released per mole of CO₂ absorbed,
−[H_L(α₂) − H_L(α₁) − (α₂ − α₁) h_CO₂^ig(T)]/(α₂ − α₁), for 1 mol MEA, with
zero calorimeter vapor inventory and an ideal-gas CO₂ feed. The neutral
records cancel between the endpoints, so the result depends only on the EOS,
the reactions and their reference chain.

# Numerical result

The serialized working record is `9055458d8b7cd767a0d08e9f37e4fd28631e29c363364d7b842ebade645cb241`, with SSM+DS model D `p5conv-a-11`, source R4 and the inherited assessed R1–R3/R5 corrections. The current wheel is `28181e72e429c6e87fc6361082af1a7b21c8747e76bda65a1c30abb4a97402f2`. All 113 retained intervals and all endpoint states evaluate; no interval is omitted.

| Cohort | Intervals scored | RMSE (kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂) | Bias (kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Kim–Svendsen 40/80 °C calibration | 66 / 66 | 8.027440 | -3.617420 |
| Kim 2014 model-selection comparison | 27 / 27 | 6.670190 | -0.252200 |
| Kim–Svendsen 120 °C comparison outside working range | 20 / 20 | 30.124813 | -13.250753 |

![Promoted-record finite-dose absorption heat at 40, 80 and 120 °C. The 120 °C values are out-of-domain comparisons.](../figures/calorimetry/output/current-selected-direct-enthalpy.svg)

# Conclusion and limits

The promoted record has 8.027440 kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂ RMSE on the 40/80 °C calibration intervals and 30.124813 kJ mol⁻¹ on the 120 °C cohort, with mean biases −3.617420 and −13.250753 kJ mol⁻¹. This is numerical verification and reported calibration/assessment evidence. It supplies no caloric or process-column qualification and does not extend the working domain beyond 30 wt% MEA at 40–80 °C. The regenerated thermal consistency checks are reported below; pure-water heat-capacity disagreement and the absence of a verified pure-MEA liquid reference remain separate limits.

The historical September-incumbent comparison on wheel `b66c7b96` evaluated 109/113 intervals: calibration RMSE 11.77 (bias +0.4), 120 °C RMSE 29.28 (bias −15.8), and Kim 2014 RMSE 10.80 (bias +1.4) kJ mol⁻¹. Those values describe `868a5018`; the new comparison changes both parameter record and producing wheel and is not a wheel-only experiment.

The regenerated enthalpy-reference checks pass 9/9 states at 40, 80 and 120 °C and loadings 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5, under the existing 1e−6 relative limits. Maximum Gibbs–Helmholtz disagreement is 3.662e-13; maximum centered-feed re-solve disagreement is 5.604e-09. Pure-water heat capacity differs by up to 15.00% and vaporization enthalpy by up to 1.34%. These are numerical consistency and pure-water comparisons, not physical qualification of loaded MEA.
